pop_methods.label: City's total, shared by actual growth
pop_methods.about: All of Calgary adds up to the City's own population estimate and forecast for that month, but growth is not spread evenly: each community is its 2021 Census count times one factor, plus the growth the growth model measured there (homes built since 2021). The factor spreads only what homes do not explain (more people per home since 2021, people in seniors' homes, residences and shelters, the Census undercount) over every community's 2021 count. Fast-building areas get their real growth; built-out ones grow less.

pop_methods.label: City's total, one rate for all
pop_methods.about: All of Calgary adds up to the City's own population estimate and forecast for that month. Communities built since 2021 keep their growth model count; every other community is its 2021 Census count grown by one factor, the same for all, so each keeps its 2021 share. The factor also brings in people the Census count of private homes leaves out (seniors' homes, residences, shelters), so its growth since 2021 reads about 3 points higher than real growth.

pop_methods.label: Growth model
pop_methods.about: The 2021 Census for each community, grown with the homes on the City's current property assessment roll (homes lived in x 2021 people per home). Follows the homes actually built.

pop_methods.label: 2021 Census, no growth
pop_methods.about: Each community's 2021 Census count (May 2021), unchanged. This is how the City's own 311 ward dashboard counts (it divides by 2021 Census households). Undercounts fast-growing communities.
